questions.q: Why is cost attribution genuinely hard on the shared `solara-train` cluster?
options: Because the cloud provider doesn't issue invoices for GPU clusters
Because both teams' jobs share the same 64 nodes in shifting proportions, so no single invoice line item shows one team's cost
Because Kubernetes doesn't support namespaces
Because GPUs can't be metered at all
questions.explain: Unlike a single-tenant setup, the ratio of training-lm to training-mm usage shifts hour to hour, so each team's cost must be reconstructed from actual resource consumption rather than read off a bill.

questions.q: What Kubernetes-native concept does Kubecost use as the primary grouping for Solara AI's per-team cost breakdown?
options: Container image tags
Namespace — since training-lm and training-mm are already separate namespaces
Node hostname only
Git commit hash of the training script
questions.explain: Because each team's jobs run in their own namespace, Kubecost's default namespace-based allocation view already separates their costs without custom instrumentation.

questions.q: How does Kubecost attribute the cost of a node's GPUs to specific pods?
options: Evenly across every pod on the cluster regardless of GPU usage
Proportional to how many GPUs each pod actually requested on that node
Only to the pod that was scheduled first
GPU cost cannot be attributed to individual pods
questions.explain: A pod requesting 8 GPUs on a node is charged that node's full GPU cost; a pod sharing a node with others is charged proportionally to its GPU request.

questions.q: What is "shared cost" in Kubecost's cost model?
options: The total cost of the entire cluster combined
Infrastructure cost like the control plane and shared monitoring stack that isn't attributable to one tenant namespace directly
The cost of GPUs only, never CPU or memory
A cost that is always split exactly 50/50 between teams
questions.explain: Shared cost covers things like the Kubernetes control plane and shared monitoring infrastructure that neither team requested directly; it's typically allocated proportional to each namespace's resource usage share, not split evenly.

questions.q: Why does the lesson connect GPU utilization monitoring (Lesson 29) to cost attribution?
options: They are unrelated topics covered together only for convenience
A team paying for GPUs but keeping them at low utilization is a cost problem as much as a performance problem
GPU utilization data is required to install Kubecost
Utilization monitoring replaces the need for cost attribution entirely
questions.explain: A team's requested GPUs are charged to them whether or not those GPUs are kept busy, so low utilization directly translates into wasted spend for that team.
